sentences.text: ORAL ORDER 1.

The present First Appeal, under Section 173 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, is preferred by the appellant - claimant, being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the judgment and award dated 27.03.2009 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Aux.), Himatnagar in Motor Accident Claim Petition No.659 of 2003, by which the Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.28,500/-
with 7.5% per annum interest to the claimant/s, holding opponents liable, jointly and severally.
2. Brief facts of the case are as under:
2.1

entities.text: Motor Accident Claim Petition No.659 of 2003
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text:
On 19/03/2003 at about 3.15 p.m., the appellant was sitting in the S.T.Depot Workshop at Bhiloda on the table of vehicle Examiner in a chair and at that time, the driver of the S.T.Bus No.GJ 18V 2135 drove his bus in front instead of reverse in a rash and negligent manner on account of which the S.T.bus dashed with the table and chair on which appellant was sitting as a result of which appellant NEUTRAL Sadat Lilaben Babubhai vs Laljibhai M Katara on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/97487663/
1 CITATION C/FA/426/2010 ORDER DATED: 12/08/2024 undefined was compressed and therefore appellant sustained serious injuries of fractures of right thigh, latent injuries on right hand and injuries on other parts of the body, he was immediately taken to Cottage Hospital, Shiloda, and then in Civil Hospital,
Himatnagar where he was admitted as indoor patient.

entities.text: NEUTRAL Sadat Lilaben Babubhai vs Laljibhai M Katara
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: That offence was registered at Bhiloda police station Cr.Reg.No.I. 28 of 2003.
Hence, claim petition has been preferred.
2.2 Notices were served to the opponents.
Only Opponent No.2 - corporation has filed its written statement at Exh.16 by disputing all the averments made by the claimant in the claim petition and also disputed the liability.
2.3 Issues have been framed by the Tribunal.
The oral as well as documentary evidence were led by the rival parties before the Tribunal.
After considering the documentary as well as oral evidence and submissions made at the bar, the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition by awarding compensation as noted above.

2.4 Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal,
the present appeal is preferred by the claimant for enhancement.
3. Learned advocate for the appellant - claimant has submitted that the Tribunal has committed an error in not properly calculating the amount of compensation.

It is submitted that amount awarded is on lower side as the Tribunal has not properly considered the various aspects; like income of the injured, injuries, prospective income, disability and negligence, special diet, transportation and attendant charges, pain, shock and suffering, actual loss, etc.

At the outset, he NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/426/2010 ORDER DATED: 12/08/2024 undefined has relied upon the decision of this Court in First Appeal No.1528 of 2009 dated 15.12.2015, has has submitted that the Tribunal has committed error in not awarding any amount towards future loss of income.

He has submitted that at the time of accident, injured was serving as helper in S.T.Corporation and getting salary of Rs.8,000/- p.m. and in spare time, by doing agriculture and other repairing work, he was earning Rs.2,000/-p.m.
Hence, in absence of any documentary evidence to proof the same, income of the injured at least Rs.5,000/- p.m. is required to considered.
Accordingly, actual loss of income may be granted considering the income of the injured at lest for 1.5 years considering the treatment and injuries of the injured.

It is submitted that considering decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited versus Pranay Shethi reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680,
as well as taking into account the age of the injured, addition to the extent of 30% may be granted in monthly income of the injured.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited versus Pranay Shethi reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is submitted that the Tribunal has not properly considered the disability certificates issued by doctor at Exh.33 and injury, whereby it is clearly stated that the claimant has sustained permanent disability to the extent 20% for body as a whole due to injuries as well as fracture on femur leg right thigh.
Therefore, the disability which should be considered by the Tribunal is to the extent 20% overall and the Tribunal ought to have granted compensation accordingly.
Furthermore, the multiplier should be 4 considering the various decisions of the Hon'ble Apex Court and taking into account the age of the claimant.

It is submitted that the Sadat Lilaben Babubhai vs Laljibhai M Katara on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/97487663/
2 Tribunal has committed an error by not properly considering the compensation under the head of pain, shock and suffering, which should be Rs.25,000/-, instead of Rs.7,500/- awarded by the Tribunal, looking to the injuries sustained by the claimant and considering the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/426/2010 ORDER DATED: 12/08/2024 undefined decisions of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of : (i) Pranay Shethi (supra) and (ii) Magma General Insurance Company Limited versus Nanu Ram and others reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is submitted that the Tribunal has committed error in not properly considering the amount towards special diet, transportation and attendant charges, which should be Rs.15,000/-considering the time of treatment taken by the injured.
It is submitted that the Tribunal has rightly awarded the compensation under different heads, except the above raised.
It is submitted that the appropriate enhancement be granted by modifying the award impugned.
It is submitted that the appeal may be allowed.
4. Per contra, learned advocate for respondent No.2 - corporation has submitted that the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is just and proper.
It is submitted that the Tribunal has rightly not awarded any amount towards future loss of income as the injured is died during the pendency of the claim petition.
Furthermore, it is submitted that the Tribunal has rightly considered the compensation towards pain, shock and suffering.
It is submitted that the Tribunal has rightly not awarded amount towards special diet, attendant charges, and attendant charges.
It is also submitted that no interference is required in the impugned award.

However, from the submissions made by learned advocate for the appellant that the Tribunal has committed certain errors, on this aspect, learned advocate for the respondent/s has submitted that if this Court feels that there is some error in calculation of the amount in view of settled position of law, in awarding compensation by the Tribunal, then the Court may pass appropriate order by considering the submissions made by him/her, in the interest of justice.
5. It is noteworthy to mention that the provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 which gives paramount importance to the concept of 'just and fair' compensation.

It is a beneficial legislation Sadat Lilaben Babubhai vs Laljibhai M Katara on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/97487663/
3 which has been framed with the object of providing relief to the victims or their families.

sentences.text: Section 168 of the Motor Vehicles Act deals with the concept of 'just compensation' which ought to be determined on the foundation of fairness, reasonableness and equitability.

Although such determination can never be arithmetically exact or perfect, an endeavor should be made by the Court to award just and fair compensation irrespective of the amount claimed by the claimant/s.
6.1
I have heard the learned advocates for the respective parties and considered the submissions made by the rival parties.
I have perused the record and proceedings of the Tribunal.
I have gone through the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.

It is noted that the claimant has by and large claimed enhancement towards income of the injured, injuries, prospective income,
disability and negligence, special diet, transportation and attendant charges, pain, shock and suffering, actual loss, etc. .
At the outset, I have considering the decision cited at the bar by learned advocate for the appellant.
The judgments cited at the bar by learned advocate for the appellant is helpful to the facts of the present case.

It is fruitful to refer the decision of this Court in First Appeal No.1528 of 2009 dated 15.12.2015, relevant paras are as under:
"4.
Thus, in the opinion of the Division Bench, even after the death of the claimant due to natural causes after filing of the claim petition, the right to sue would survive in the heirs of the claimant.

However, this would be to the limited extent of loss of estate of the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/426/2010 ORDER DATED: 12/08/2024 undefined deceased which would include personal expenses incurred on the treatment and other claim related to the loss to the estate.

In the judgement, the Division Bench referred to and noted with approval the decision of learned Single Judge in case of Jenabai widow of Abdul Karim Musa vs. Gujarat State Road Transport Corporation reported in 1991 (1) GLR 352.

entities.text: Abdul Karim Musa vs. Gujarat State Road Transport Corporation reported in 1991 (1) GLR 352
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In such decision, this aspect was further elaborated, as noted by the Division Bench in the referral judgement, as under:
"9.02.

Identical question came to be considered by the learned Single Judge in the case of Jenabai Widow of Abdul Karim Musa (supra) and in para 15, the learned Single Judge has observed and held that loss to the estate or injury to the proprietary or property right affecting the estate of the deceased cannot be said to have been covered by exception contained in section 306 of the Indian Succession Act and it is held that right to sue is available to the legal representatives of the deceased, as a claim on account of the deceased survive and passed over to his legal representatives.

In the aforesaid decision it is held that expenses incurred on treatment or loss of income from the date of incident to death amounts to a loss to the estate."
5.

Thus, the ratio of the Division Bench that could be culled out is that even after the death of the claimant, after filing of the claim petition, the right to sue would survive in the legal representative which would be extended to the loss to estate and in terms of the decision of the learned Single Judge in case of Jenabai Widow of Abdul Karim Musa vs. Gujarat State Road Transport Corporation (Supra).

entities.text: Jenabai Widow of Abdul Karim Musa vs. Gujarat State Road Transport Corporation
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This in turn, would include the expenses incurred on treatment or loss of income from the date of accident to death.

4 6.

sentences.text:
Applying such principles in the case on hand, I may notice that the claimant was engaged in the business of selling waste cloth and NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/426/2010 ORDER DATED:
12/08/2024 undefined claimed to be earning Rs. 100/- per day.
She was aged about 45 years.
Even without granting future rise in income on such uncertain business, her income could be safely adopted at Rs. 3000/- per month.
Applying agreed disability of 20%, her monthly loss of income would be Rs. 600/- or Rs. 7200/- per annum.
She survived for 11 years post accident.
The claimants would, therefore, receive additional compensation of Rs. 79,200/- towards future loss of income till her death.
Such amount shall be paid with simple interest @8% from the date of claim petition till actual payment.
Appeal is allowed and disposed of accordingly.
R & P to be transmitted back to the Trial Court."
6.2 In view of the above, future loss of income is required to be considered.

Considering the above-mentioned decision as well as considering the fact that at the time of accident, injured was serving as helper in S.T.Corporation and getting salary of Rs.8,000/-p.m. and in spare time, by doing agriculture and other repairing work, he was earning Rs.2,000/- p.m.
Hence, in absence of any documentary evidence to proof the same, income of the injured at least Rs.5,000/- p.m. is required to considered.

Furthermore, considering various above-mentioned judgments of the Hon'ble Apex and taking into account the age of the claimant at the time of accident, i.e., 45 years,
addition to the extent of 30% is required to be granted in the monthly income.
Therefore, it would come to Rs.6,500/- towards prospective income.

Looking to the injuries and the disability certificates issued by doctor at Exh.33 and injury, whereby it is clearly stated that the claimant has sustained permanent disability to the extent 20% for body as a whole due to injuries as well as fracture on femur leg right thigh.
Therefore, the disability which should be considered by the Tribunal is to the extent 20% overall and the Tribunal ought to have granted compensation accordingly.

Furthermore, Considering the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/426/2010 ORDER DATED:
12/08/2024 undefined various decisions of the Hon'ble Apex Court, and taking into account the age of the injured at the time of accident i.e. 45 years at the time of accident, and well as taking into account the fact that the injured is died during the pendency of the claim petition, hence, multiplier of 4 is required to be granted.
Therefore, Rs.6,500/- x 20% x 12 (annual) x 4 (multiplier) would come to Rs.62,400/- which would be the future loss of income of the claimant.

6.3 Furthermore, actual loss of income should be Rs.85,000/-, considering the monthly income Rs.5,000/- of the claimant for 1.5 years months as well as taking into accoutn the peculiar facts of the case.

Furthermore, the Tribunal has erred in awarding Rs.7,500/- towards pain, shock and suffering, which should be Rs.25,000/- considering the injuries and treatment as well as taking into account various decisions of the Hon'ble Apex Court.

Furthermore, towards special diet, attendant and transportation charges, Rs.15,000/- is required to be awarded considering the injuries and period of hospitalization of the claimant, as well as treatment taken by the injured.

Furthermore,
under the other heads, the amount awarded by the Tribunal are not disputed by the claimant in the present case.
Otherwise also, the Tribunal has rightly considered the amount of compensation under other heads.
6.4 Thus, the appellant - claimant is entitled to get the following final amount as compensation :
